rationale: The pipeline detrended both the exit-probability series X_t (eq. 5) and the time-aggregation-ignoring X-tilde_t (eq. 6 with F-tilde=F) with an HP filter (smoothing 1e5) and reported the standard deviations in summary.json. For the paper's headline 1948:M1-2010:M12 sample (output/two_state_1948_2010/summary.json), sd_detrended_X = 0.0768 and sd_detrended_Xtilde = 0.1086, which round to the paper's reported 0.07 and 0.11 respectively; the replication log for this run notes 'sd_detrended_X=0.0768 (paper ~0.07)'. X-tilde_t is essentially exact (0.1086 vs 0.11, ~1.3% off) and X_t is within ~10% (0.0768 vs 0.07), well inside the small-value band given the paper's 2-decimal reporting and the documented post-2005 data reconstruction (fix_severity.json: a major but conservative tail-splice to extend the shipped share window). The qualitative point of the footnote — that ignoring time aggregation inflates measured volatility (X-tilde_t std clearly exceeds X_t std, ratio ~1.4 vs paper's ~1.6) — is reproduced. The shipped-data-only 1951-2005 run (output/two_state/summary.json) gives the same ordering with slightly lower magnitudes (0.0654 and 0.0965). Both runs support the claim; the full-sample run matches the paper's stated values closely.
